Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

against preposition

opposing; as a defence from

also versus, against the current, protection against, against my will

classical

Publil. Sent. R 27: remedium … contrā fulmen
Cic. Att. 13.38.1: cum scrīberem contrā Epicūrēōs

contrā + acc.

preposition with the accusative; also an adverb, “opposite, in return”

The general word: against a person, a current, a wish (contrā voluntātem).

Other words

  • adversus (adversum) + acc. — against (an opponent); as a defence against

    preposition with the accusative · also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 8.5: domus mūnīmentum sit adversus īnfesta temporis; Tac. Germ. 46.5–6: sēcūrī adversus hominēs, sēcūrī adversus deōs

    Literally “turned towards”: so also, of conduct, “towards” someone.

  • in + acc. — against (of hostile words, feelings and acts)

    preposition with the accusative · also used · classical · Cic. ND 3.84: ad impietātem in deōs, in hominēs adjūnxit injūriam (Lewis & Short)

    Of words, feelings and acts aimed at someone; the same construction serves for kind ones, “towards”.

Examples

  • Remedium frūstrā est contrā fulmen quaerere.

    It is no use looking for a remedy against lightning.Publil. Sent. R 27

  • ante lūcem cum scrīberem contrā Epicūrēōs, dē eōdem oleō et operā exarāvī nesciō quid ad tē et ante lūcem dedī

    before dawn, while I was writing against the Epicureans, I scribbled something to you by the same lamp and with the same effort, and sent it off before daylightCic. Att. 13.38.1

  • obsequiō trānantur aquae: nec vincere possīs flūmina, sī contrā, quam rapit unda, natēs

    you get across water by giving way to it; you could not beat a river if you swam against the way the current pullsOv. Ars 2.181–182

  • cibus famem sēdet, pōtiō sitim exstinguat, vestis arceat frīgus, domus mūnīmentum sit adversus īnfesta temporis

    let food still hunger, drink quench thirst, clothes keep out the cold, and a house be a shelter against bad weatherSen. Ep. 8.5

  • Menēnius Agrippa plēbem cum patribus in grātiam trāditur redūxisse nōtā illā dē membrīs hūmānīs adversus ventrem discordantibus fābulā

    Menenius Agrippa is said to have reconciled the people with the senators by that famous fable of the parts of the body quarrelling against the bellyQuint. 5.11.19

See also enemy.

SourcesLewis & Short: contra · Lewis & Short: adversus · Lewis & Short: in
